support.claim: With Email Format: Both, n8n sends both formats and the email recipient's client chooses which format to display.
Attachments can be added under Options → Attachments in the Send Email node.

grade.rationale: The agent accurately answers all parts of the user's inquiry, explaining that n8n sends both the HTML and plain-text parts together (multipart/alternative) and leaves the choice to the recipient's email client. It also correctly validates the user's strategy of including the QR code as a file attachment as the ideal fallback.

support.claim: In Workflow Settings, setting 'Save execution progress' allows the workflow to resume from where it stopped in case of an error.
An error workflow starts with an Error Trigger node and is configured in Workflow Settings.
Partial executions can fail with 'Existing execution data is too large', which can be mitigated with a Limit node during testing.
Out-of-memory errors in n8n can produce messages like 'Execution stopped at this node (n8n may have run out of memory while executing it)'.

grade.rationale: The reply directly answers the user's architectural questions regarding checkpoints, retries, and error recovery. It correctly recommends built-in settings ('Save execution progress'), Error Trigger workflows, durable checkpointing, and idempotent operations, matching the accepted solution and official documentation.

support.claim: The production webhook runs the published version of the workflow, not what is currently in the editor draft.
Production executions won't reflect editor changes until the workflow is published.
Manual executions can substitute pinned data, but production executions ignore pinned data.
The test webhook URL works with 'Listen for Test Event' and displays data in the editor, whereas the production URL registers when published.

grade.rationale: The reply correctly identifies the core mechanism: in n8n, production webhook executions execute the published version of the workflow rather than the autosaved draft in the editor. It provides clear, actionable guidance to publish the workflow to make the updates live.

grade.material_error_what: Recommends using the built-in OpenAI Audio Transcribe node which does not support diarization, and treats the issue as an insurmountable UI limitation instead of directing the user to use the HTTP Request node to call the OpenAI audio transcriptions endpoint.

support.claim: The OpenAI Audio node only supports transcription and translation operations using Whisper by default.
The AI Agent prompt expects text input rather than binary file data.
The OpenAI node does not allow selecting the gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize model for transcription.

grade.rationale: The customer specifically asked how to transcribe an audio file with speaker diarization using the gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize model, noting that the built-in Whisper node does not support diarization. The reply correctly explains why the AI Agent failed with binary input, but then advises falling back to the standard OpenAI Audio node (which cannot diarize) rather than providing the solution of using an HTTP Request node to call the OpenAI API directly.

support.claim: MySQL nodes use MySQL credentials.
Credentials in n8n are tested upon saving.
Credentials are scoped to a specific project or personal space.

grade.rationale: The reply correctly identifies that the credential ID lookup error stems from project vs. personal space scoping issues and advises verifying the scope and recreating the credential in the node. It also offers escalation to support or the forum if the issue persists.

support.claim: The community forum provides free support for all n8n users.
Users on non-Enterprise Cloud plans should use the forum for technical support, while email support is for admin and billing.
Enterprise customers can use email support for technical, account, billing, and other inquiries.
Debug information can be copied from Help → About n8n → Copy debug information.
Workflows shared in the community forum should be wrapped in code blocks with triple backticks.

grade.rationale: The reply partially answers the prompt by identifying key items to include when asking for help (debug info from Help > About and sharing workflows inside code blocks), but misses emphasizing the full error details from the node output. It also redundantly suggests asking in the community forum even though the post is already a community forum draft.

support.claim: In queue mode, the webhook request is received by the main/webhook process and execution is passed to a worker.
N8N_CONCURRENCY_PRODUCTION_LIMIT controls the number of concurrent production executions in regular mode.
Queue mode requires Redis and a database, and running it over SQLite is not supported.
The Webhook node supports returning data generated in the workflow.

grade.rationale: The reply accurately identifies the standard solution for webhook deduplication: using an insert-first or upsert pattern against a unique constraint on `event_id` in the database, and responding to the webhook quickly. It clearly explains how to handle downstream side effects and offers a concrete workflow pattern.

support.claim: Salesforce credentials in n8n support both JWT and OAuth2.
External Client Apps are recommended for new integrations because Salesforce is deprecating Connected Apps.
Existing Connected Apps will continue to work.

grade.rationale: The reply correctly confirms the key fact from the reference packet that existing Connected Apps will continue to work, meaning migration is not immediately urgent. However, it only partially resolves the inquiry because it cannot confirm how credentials and nodes work globally across workflows, and it directs the user to multiple support routes.

grade.material_error_what: Attributes the issue to project separation/sharing and advises moving workflows and data tables into the same project, rather than addressing the workflow caller policy (N8N_WORKFLOW_CALLER_POLICY_DEFAULT_OPTION=any).

support.claim: Moving workflows or credentials removes all existing sharing.
Reviews and publishing do not cover data tables or credentials.

grade.rationale: The reply misdiagnoses the issue as a project-sharing separation and suggests moving items into the same project. In community self-hosted n8n, sub-workflow execution errors after transferring ownership are caused by the caller policy defaulting to workflows from the same owner, which requires setting N8N_WORKFLOW_CALLER_POLICY_DEFAULT_OPTION=any on the container.
The agent does not provide a fix or workaround for this known bug. Instead, it hands off the issue to multiple external channels (GitHub, n8n support, and the community forum).

support.claim: In a node's INPUT or OUTPUT panel, Search can visually filter rows or objects.
In the node details panel, users can choose between Schema, Table, and JSON views to inspect data.

grade.rationale: The reply correctly identifies that the issue appears to be a UI regression or unannounced change across workflows. It properly executes a clean handoff to n8n Cloud support while providing safe workaround suggestions (using JSON/Schema views or search) and a concise handoff summary.

support.claim: Allowing external users to log in and create or edit workflows is prohibited under the community license.
Allowing users to receive outputs or trigger prebuilt automations without access to the n8n interface is permitted.
Running n8n behind the scenes as an internal tool supporting your own product or API is permitted.
Triggering prebuilt workflows via custom APIs or webhooks rather than the n8n editor is permitted.

grade.rationale: The reply accurately identifies the core licensing rule: users cannot be given direct access to create or edit workflows, but can trigger prebuilt workflows or receive outputs. However, because the customer explicitly stated they plan to send invitation links so users can build workflows with their API, asking whether users will get UI access asks for information already provided and delays giving a definitive verdict.

grade.material_error_what: Recommending Human-in-the-loop (HITL) for tool calls to solve the issue of the agent ignoring tools. HITL pauses workflow execution for manual human approval when a tool is invoked; it does not force an LLM to call a tool, and inserting human review steps breaks an automated social media bot.

support.claim: Human-in-the-loop for AI tool calls allows adding human review before a tool executes by clicking the + icon on the tool connection.
Max Iterations defaults to 10 on the Tools Agent.
Enable Streaming requires a trigger that supports streaming responses like Chat Trigger or Webhook in Streaming mode.
The Conversational AI Agent is deprecated from n8n 1.82.0 and removed in n8n 3.0 in favor of Tools Agent.
AI Agent Tool node has an option to Require Specific Output Format.

grade.rationale: The customer is experiencing tool-calling failures and timeouts using Gemini 2.5 Flash on an automated Instagram/Facebook bot. The accepted solution points out that the issue stems from the chosen model's tool-calling reliability and recommends switching to a top-tier model (such as Claude) alongside output validation and guardrails. Instead, the reply mistakenly suggests n8n's Human-in-the-loop approval feature to force tool usage, which does not make an agent call a tool and would halt an automated customer support bot pending manual intervention.

support.claim: Verified community nodes can be installed from the nodes panel, but unverified community nodes are not available on n8n Cloud.
Submitting a node for verification by n8n is the only way to make custom nodes available on Cloud.
Nodes submitted for verification must be published to npm with a GitHub Actions workflow and provenance statement.
Nodes must be submitted through the n8n Creator Portal for verification.
Verified community nodes must adhere to technical and UX guidelines and cannot use runtime dependencies.

grade.rationale: The reply directly and accurately answers the customer's question regarding how to build, publish, and submit community nodes for verification so they can be used on n8n Cloud. It correctly outlines the entire process, including technical constraints and submission via the Creator Portal.

support.claim: The Microsoft Outlook node documentation covers authentication, supported mail operations, and government cloud settings.
The Send Email node documentation explains attachments.

grade.rationale: The agent declines to answer the user's question, stating that the provided documentation excerpts do not contain information on inline images. It offers no fix or guidance on using hosted URLs versus Base64 or CID, and breaks character by referencing the excerpts.

The agent executes a pure handoff without attempting any troubleshooting or fix. It does not mention task runners or the n8n 2.0 breaking changes regarding native Python execution. Additionally, it directs the user to several support routes instead of choosing one.

support.claim: n8n has a templates library you can browse for free workflows and examples.
Selecting Templates opens the templates library, which takes you to Workflows on the n8n website.
n8n Academy offers interactive courses with hands-on exercises and quizzes without needing external accounts for most courses.

grade.rationale: The reply correctly directs the customer to n8n's built-in template library and n8n Academy for free workflow examples and hands-on learning. However, it is partial because it overlooks the customer's concern about paid plans by not mentioning that they can self-host n8n's Community edition for free while learning. It also offers a secondary handoff to both the forum and support without choosing one route.

support.claim: n8n chat memory is session-based and does not automatically persist between sessions.
The MongoDB Chat Memory node uses the Session Key parameter to identify the session.
Context Window Length controls the number of previous interactions to consider for context.
n8n AI agent nodes can use memory, but AI chains cannot.

grade.rationale: The reply correctly validates the user's intuition that n8n chat memory is session-bound via the Session Key. However, it only partially answers the customer's request regarding advanced/long-term memory patterns (semantic/episodic), as it does not mention the Chat Memory Manager or vector store retrieval approaches shown in the reference solution.

support.claim: Setting N8N_DEFAULT_BINARY_DATA_MODE to filesystem saves binary data to disk instead of memory for single-instance setups.
n8n does not support filesystem binary data mode with queue mode, requiring database or other modes.
Using Split in Batches with sub-workflows reduces memory consumption because sub-workflows hold data only for the current batch.
Disabling saving of successful production executions helps reduce execution data storage and memory overhead.
n8n Cloud plans have fixed memory limits ranging from 320MiB RAM up to 4096MiB RAM.

grade.rationale: The reply directly answers the customer's architectural questions regarding large file processing. It recommends storing files externally and passing references, splitting execution into batches using sub-workflows, and configuring binary data mode or execution data saving depending on hosting setup. It accurately distinguishes between self-hosted and cloud environments.

grade.material_error_what: Attributes the issue to gaps, breaks, or inconsistencies in the sheet layout rather than the non-atomic nature of concurrent Google Sheets API calls, sending the user to inspect sheet formatting instead of resolving the concurrency.

support.claim: The Google Sheets node append endpoint can misalign or misplace rows if there are gaps or breaks in the data.
All executions showing Success in n8n does not guarantee rows landed where expected in Sheets.

grade.rationale: The reply correctly identifies that concurrency is causing issues and vaguely suggests queueing incoming webhook events to serialize writes. However, it fails to provide a concrete implementation (such as introducing a Wait node with a staggered delay or offloading to a database/queue) and misleads the user into thinking the issue is caused by gaps/breaks in the spreadsheet layout.
